title: Decision: Participation of the OPCW in the United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund
text:
CS-2024-4989(E) distributed 27/11/2024 
*CS-2024-4989.E* 
 
 
OPCW 
Conference of the States Parties 
Twenty-Ninth Session 
25 – 29 November 2024 
 
C-29/DEC.9 
25 November 2024 
Original: ENGLISH 
 
DECISION 
PARTICIPATION OF THE OPCW  
IN THE UNITED NATIONS JOINT STAFF PENSION FUND 
The Conference of the States Parties, 
 
Having considered the Note by the Technical Secretariat (the Secretariat) entitled 
“Participation of the OPCW in the United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund” (EC-107/S/6, 
dated 20 September 2024);  
Recalling that the Conference of the States Parties (the Conference), in a decision at its 
Twenty-Eighth Session (C-28/DEC.8, dated 27 November 2023), authorised the Secretariat to 
conclude an agreement to join the United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund (UNJSPF), from  
1 January 2025, subject to terms that the Director-General deems satisfactory and to final 
approval by the Conference at its Twenty-Ninth Session, noting that such membership would 
not require any increase in the budget of the Organisation compared to the cost of maintaining 
the current Provident Fund arrangements, and tasked the Secretariat with taking all the 
necessary preparatory administrative actions to facilitate the OPCW’s potential membership in 
the UNJSPF, anticipated for 1 January 2025, including the submission of amendments to the 
Staff and Financial Regulations for approval by the Conference at its Twenty-Ninth Session, 
as well as necessary changes to the Charter and Administrative Rules of the Provident Fund of 
the OPCW; 
Recalling also Staff Regulation 12.1, which states that “[t]he present Staff Regulations may be 
supplemented or amended by the Conference of the States Parties, without prejudice to the 
existing contracts of staff members”;  
Noting that membership in the UNJSPF would be cost-neutral for the OPCW and would not 
require any increase in the budget of the Organisation;  
Noting also that the Executive Council, in a decision at its 107th Session (EC-107/DEC.6, 
dated 8 October 2024), made recommendations on this matter to the Conference at its 
Twenty-Ninth Session, and approved amendments to the Staff Rules and to the Charter and 
Administrative Rules of the Provident Fund of the OPCW, which shall enter into force on  
1 January 2025, subject to the Conference at its Twenty-Ninth Session adopting the proposed 
amendments to the Staff Regulations effective 1 January 2025 and to the United Nations 
General Assembly deciding to admit the OPCW to membership in the UNJSPF; and

Noting further that, pursuant to Article 1 of the draft proposed “Agreement between the 
United Nations Joint Staff Pension Board and the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical 
Weapons as to the Conditions Governing the Admission of the Organisation for the Prohibition 
of Chemical Weapons to Membership in the United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund”  
(Annex 1 hereto), which would enter into effect on 1 January 2025 should the OPCW be 
admitted to membership in the UNJSPF, “the OPCW accepts the Regulations, Rules and 
Pension Adjustment System of the UNJSPF, as they are in force on that date and as they may 
be amended from time to time thereafter”, and that Article 6, paragraph (c), of the UNJSPF 
Regulations requires that “[e]ach member organization shall make rules for the election or 
appointment of the members and alternate members of its staff pension committee”; 
Hereby: 
1. 
Approves the draft proposed “Agreement between the United Nations Joint Staff 
Pension Board and the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons as to the 
Conditions Governing the Admission of the Organisation for the Prohibition of 
Chemical Weapons to Membership in the United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund” 
(Annex 1 hereto) and authorises the Director-General to sign it on behalf of the OPCW, 
subject to the United Nations General Assembly deciding to admit the OPCW to 
membership in the UNJSPF; 
2. 
Adopts the amendments to the Staff Regulations of the OPCW (Annex 2 hereto), which 
shall enter into force on 1 January 2025, subject to the United Nations General 
Assembly deciding to admit the OPCW to membership in the UNJSPF; 
3. 
Requests the Director-General to take all the necessary administrative actions to 
implement the proposed “Agreement between the United Nations Joint Staff Pension 
Board and the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons as to the 
Conditions Governing the Admission of the Organisation for the Prohibition of 
Chemical Weapons to Membership in the United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund”, 
and to establish the OPCW’s staff pension committee; and 
4. 
Authorises the Chairperson of the Conference, in consultation with the General 
Committee, to select from among the members of delegations of States Parties, one 
delegate as member, and a second delegate as alternate member, to represent the 
Conference in the staff pension committee to be established by the Director-General.

Pension Fund”

Annex 1 
DRAFT PROPOSED  
“AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE UNITED NATIONS JOINT STAFF PENSION 
BOARD AND THE ORGANISATION FOR THE PROHIBITION OF CHEMICAL 
WEAPONS AS TO THE CONDITIONS GOVERNING THE ADMISSION OF THE 
ORGANISATION FOR THE PROHIBITION OF CHEMICAL WEAPONS TO 
MEMBERSHIP IN THE UNITED NATIONS JOINT STAFF PENSION FUND” 
WHEREAS the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (hereinafter 
referred to as “OPCW”) is an international, intergovernmental organization which was 
established on 29 April 1997; 
 
WHEREAS the Regulations of the United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund (hereinafter 
referred to as the “UNJSPF”), as adopted by the United Nations General Assembly and 
presently in force, provide in Article 3, paragraph (b), that “membership in the Fund shall be 
open to the specialized agencies referred to in Article 57, paragraph 2, of the Charter of the 
United Nations and to any other international, intergovernmental organization which 
participates in the common system of salaries, allowances and other conditions of service of 
the United Nations and the specialized agencies”, and in Article 3, paragraph (c), that 
“admission to membership in the [UNJSPF] shall be by decision of the General Assembly, upon 
the affirmative recommendation of the [United Nations Joint Staff Pension] Board, after 
acceptance by the organization concerned of these Regulations and agreement reached with 
the Board as to the conditions which shall govern its admission”; 
 
WHEREAS on 12 December 2022 the Director-General of the OPCW formally 
requested the UNJSPF to examine the possible admission of the OPCW to the UNJSPF; 
 
WHEREAS the Conference of States Parties (hereinafter referred to as the 
“Conference”), at its twenty-eighth session held from 27 November 2023 to 1 December 2023, 
authorized the OPCW Secretariat to conclude an agreement to join the UNJSPF from 1 January 
2025, subject to terms that the OPCW Director-General deemed satisfactory and to final 
approval by the Conference at its twenty-ninth session; 
 
WHEREAS on 28 May 2024 the Director of Administration of the OPCW submitted, 
to the UNJSPF: (i) information on how the OPCW implements the common system of salaries, 
allowances and benefits and other conditions of service of the United Nations and the 
specialized agencies; and (ii) confirmation, subject to the conclusion of a membership 
agreement, that the OPCW undertakes to meet all the conditions for membership, including 
acceptance of the UNJSPF Regulations and Rules and acceptance of the jurisdiction of the 
United Nations Appeals Tribunal in respect of pension matters; 
 
WHEREAS the OPCW has provided, to the UNJSPF Pension Administration 
(hereinafter referred to as the “Pension Administration”), its proposed amendments to the 
OPCW Staff Regulations and Rules to accommodate membership in the UNJSPF and the 
Pension Administration has provided comments thereon;

WHEREAS it has been verified by the International Civil Service Commission that the 
OPCW generally follows the provisions of the common system of salaries, allowances and 
other conditions of service of the United Nations and the specialized agencies; 
 
WHEREAS, at its seventy-eighth session held from 28 July 2024 to 2 August 2024 the 
United Nations Joint Staff Pension Board (hereinafter the “Board”) decided to recommend to 
the United Nations General Assembly that the OPCW be admitted to membership in the 
UNJSPF effective 1 January 2025, subject to (a) the Conference confirming its approval of the 
OPCW joining the UNJSPF effective 1 January 2025, (b) the draft amended OPCW Staff 
Regulations and Rules entering into force on or prior to 1 January 2025 in substantially the 
form received by the Pension Administration, incorporating any comments provided thereon 
by the Pension Administration, and (c) the conclusion of the terms of an agreement between 
the OPCW and the Board, to be signed by the Chief Executive of Pension Administration on 
behalf of the Board, substantially in the same terms as recent agreements concluded with new 
member organizations and specifically addressing the OPCW’s acceptance of the UNJSPF 
Regulations and Rules, including the jurisdiction of the United Nations Appeals Tribunal in 
respect of pension matters; 
 
WHEREAS, at its Twenty-Ninth Session held from 25 to 29 November 2024, the 
Conference confirmed [its approval of the terms of membership in the UNJSPF and changes to 
the OPCW Regulations and Rules]; 
 
WHEREAS the United Nations General Assembly, by its resolution 79/xxx dated xxx 
approved this recommendation of the Board and decided to admit the OPCW to membership 
in the UNSPF effective 1 January 2025; 
 
NOW THEREFORE the parties hereto agree as follows: 
 
 
Article 1 
Acceptance of UNJSPF Regulations, Rules and Pension Adjustment System 
 
1.1 Effective 1 January 2025, the OPCW accepts the Regulations, Rules and Pension 
Adjustment System of the UNJSPF, as they are in force on that date and as they may be 
amended from time to time thereafter. 
 
 
Article 2 
Participation 
 
2.1 Subject to the provisions of this Article, all staff members of the OPCW in service at the 
time when this Agreement enters into effect shall become participants in the UNJSPF from 
1 January 2025 unless their participation is expressly excluded by the terms of their 
appointment in accordance with article 21(a) of the UNJSPF Regulations. 
 
2.2 Any staff member of the OPCW who has reached the age of 60 on 1 January 2025 may 
exercise a one-time option not to participate in the UNJSPF. The OPCW shall provide the 
UNJSPF with a list of those staff members who are over the age of 60 on 1 January 2025 and 
who opt not to participate in the UNJSPF.

Annex 1 
page 5 
 
 
2.3 Any staff member of the OPCW who is irrevocably set to separate from the OPCW on or 
before 30 June 2025 may exercise a one-time option not to participate in the UNJSPF. The 
OPCW shall provide the UNJSPF with a list of those staff members who are irrevocably set to 
separate on or before 30 June 2025 and who opt not to participate in the UNJSPF. 
 
2.4 Those staff members of the OPCW who are eligible to join the UNJSPF as of 1 January 
2025 and who exercise the one-time option not to participate, as provided in Articles 2.2 
and 2.3, shall not have the option to join the UNJSPF at a later date while still employed by the 
OPCW. 
 
 
Article 3 
Transfer of Provident Fund balances 
 
3.1 Staff members of the OPCW who enter the UNJSPF as participants on 1 January 2025 may 
exercise a one-time election to transfer their full Provident Fund balance to the UNJSPF. In the 
event of such an election, contributory service in the UNJSPF shall be accorded to the 
individual participants in accordance with article 22(c) of the UNJPSF Regulations on the basis 
set out below. 
 
3.2 Upon a written election by an OPCW participant made on or before 31 March 2025 on a 
form provided for that purpose by the UNJSPF, the OPCW shall pay to the UNJSPF, upon 
request from the UNJSPF and no later than 31 May 2025, an amount equal to the participant’s 
full Provident Fund account balance, including any interest and investment gains attributable 
to the account, subject to Article 3.4. The OPCW shall also provide the UNJSPF with the 
breakdown of the Provident Fund account balances corresponding to the employee and 
employer contributions for each participant who provides a written election to transfer his or 
her balance, as well as information regarding the participant’s prior UNJSPF participation(s), 
if known. 
 
3.3 The amount paid to the UNJSPF by the OPCW shall be converted by the UNJSPF into 
United States dollars using the United Nations operational rate of exchange in effect on the date 
of the payment. On the basis of this amount, the participant shall be credited with contributory 
service in the UNJSPF equal to such period as may be determined, by the UNJSPF Consulting 
Actuary and in accordance with the actuarial assumptions applied by the UNJSPF and the 
relevant articles of the UNJSPF Regulations, to be equal in value to the amount paid to the 
UNJSPF by the OPCW. For the purpose of this calculation, the UNJSPF Consulting Actuary 
shall use the participant’s nearest age and pensionable remuneration as of 31 March 2025. The 
pensionable remuneration will be converted into United States dollars using the United Nations 
operational rate of exchange in effect on 31 March 2025, when applicable. The participant’s 
UNJSPF account shall also be credited with the amount of the employee’s contributions to the 
Provident Fund, including any interest and investment gains attributable to the account, as 
converted into United States dollars using the United Nations operational rate of exchange in 
effect on the date of the payment.

Annex 1 
page 6 
 
 
3.4 Notwithstanding the above, the maximum contributory service credit granted in the 
UNJSPF by application of this Article shall not exceed the length of the actual past service that 
the participant had performed as a staff member of the OPCW prior to 1 January 2025. For the 
purpose of calculating the length of actual past service, any periods of leave without pay during 
which the staff member made concurrent contributions to the Provident Fund shall be included; 
periods of leave without pay during which the staff member did not make concurrent 
contributions to the Provident Fund shall be excluded. After calculating the actuarial value 
determining the amount required for the maximum available recognition of past service, only 
the amount required for the maximum available recognition will be transferred by the OPCW 
to the UNJSPF. Any excess amount transferred to the UNJSPF will be returned to the OPCW. 
Any excess amount will not be credited to the participant’s UNJSPF account. 
 
3.5 The OPCW shall be responsible for providing accurate and timely information with regard 
to the staff members and their Provident Fund balances, as well as for paying all fees of the 
UNJSPF Consulting Actuary as they relate to the calculations referred to in this Article. 
 
 
Article 4 
Jurisdiction of the United Nations Appeals Tribunal 
 
4.1 
The OPCW accepts, effective 1 January 2025, the jurisdiction of the United Nations 
Appeals Tribunal to hear and pass final judgement on applications from staff members or 
former staff members of the OPCW alleging non-observance of the UNJSPF Regulations, 
arising out of decisions of the Standing Committee on behalf of the Board. 
 
 
Article 5 
Entry fee 
 
5.1 Upon entry into force of this Agreement, a flat fee of USD 25,000, as well as a fee of 
USD 20 per new participant, shall be paid by the OPCW to the UNJSPF.  Once the OPCW has 
joined, it will cover its own administrative expenses, in accordance with article 15(c) of the 
UNJSPF Regulations. 
 
 
Article 6 
Termination of transfer agreement 
 
6.1 Upon entry into force of this Agreement, the transfer agreement between the UNJSPF and 
the OPCW dated 1 January 2013 shall terminate, except that the UNJSPF shall continue to 
honour, on the same terms as stipulated in the transfer agreement, transfers of pension rights 
from the OPCW to the UNJSPF for former staff members of the OPCW who separated from 
the service of the OPCW on or before 31 December 2024 and who enter participation in the 
Fund within one year of their separation.

Article 7 
Entry into force 
 
7.1 The present Agreement shall enter into force on signature with effect from 1 January 2025.
